speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Given your history of AIDS, it is crucial we determine the duration of your floaters and spots to rule out opportunistic infections like CMV retinitis. Can you tell me exactly when these visual symptoms started and if they have been getting worse rapidly?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of decreased vision and seeing black spots in the right eye. He reports no pain, and the left eye is asymptomatic. He mentions being treated for fungal esophagitis 6 months ago and was diagnosed with Kaposi's sarcoma 2 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a very important detail; a 2-day history of painless vision loss in an AIDS patient is highly concerning for CMV retinitis. To assess the severity of his immunosuppression, what is his most recent CD4 count and HIV viral load?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Decreased vision and black spots in the right eye. I also have No pain, Left eye is asymptomatic.

speaker: Doctor
text: To help pinpoint the cause, have you noticed any photopsia (flashes of light) or a shadow in your peripheral vision? Additionally, are you currently on antiretroviral therapy, and if so, when did you start it?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: AIDS, fungal esophagitis treated with fluconazole, Kaposi's sarcoma Social history: No additional information provided

speaker: Doctor
text: The lack of pain and flashes makes retinal detachment less likely, strongly pointing toward an opportunistic infection like CMV retinitis given his AIDS history. REQUEST TEST: Fundoscopy.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Granular yellow-white opacities around the retinal vessels and multiple areas of dot-blot hemorrhages

speaker: Doctor
text: The fundoscopy findings of granular yellow-white opacities and hemorrhages are pathognomonic for Cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis in this context. DIAGNOSIS READY: CMV retinitis
